answer:
Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) for the implementation.
Solve the quasi-incompressible finite-strain hyperelasticity problem with a mixed displacement-pressure (u, p) formulation consistent with plane strain quasi-incompressibility.
The domain Ω is the rectangle (0, 1.0) x (0, 0.20) m with two circular holes of radius a = 0.04 m centred at (0.40, 0.10) m and (0.60, 0.10) m.
Generate a mesh of this geometry, e.g. with a coarse-to-moderate unstructured triangular mesh (mesh size around 0.005-0.01 m near holes is acceptable).
Material model: isotropic quasi-incompressible neo-Hookean with Young's modulus E = 5 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.49, used in the mixed formulation in plane strain.
Solve the nonlinear problem using Newton's method with a standard continuation/stepwise loading ramp (e.g. ramp the prescribed displacement and hole pressure in uniform increments) until the full load is reached.
Left edge (x = 0): prescribe u_x = 0 and u_y = 0 (fully fixed).
Right edge (x = 1.0): prescribe u_x = 0.060 m and u_y = 0, applied via a ramped Dirichlet boundary condition on u_x with u_y = 0.
Top and bottom edges (y = 0 and y = 0.20): traction-free.
Each hole boundary: apply a uniform follower pressure of magnitude P_hole = 0.10 MPa using the reference (undeformed) hole normals, i.e. use the outward normal of the initial geometry rather than the current deformed normal in the pressure traction term; the pressure magnitude is still scaled by the load ramp and applied on the deformed surface measure (current area element).
Assemble the weak form with the pressure traction term written as an integral over the hole boundaries using the reference normal and the deformation-gradient-based area factor appropriate for a pressure load in the current configuration.
Use a Taylor-Hood type mixed element, e.g. quadratic (P2) displacement and linear (P1) pressure, with proper stabilization-free inf-sup compatible pairing.
Post-process the Cauchy stress from the converged solution and compute the von Mises stress.
Save a colour map (filled contour plot) of the pressure field p as q14_p.png.
Save a colour map of the von Mises stress as q14_vm.png.
Save the displacement field u in XDMF format (with a matching HDF5 backend).
Label the plots appropriately and use consistent units of MPa and metres.
